title: Adding shared filter fields to MCP query kinds touches schema, generated files and one test per runner
answers: what to regenerate after changing MCP analytics query schema
add filter field to MCPTool query kind
services/mcp generated mcp_analytics.ts out of date
body:
Adding a field to an MCP query kind means changing these together:
- frontend/src/queries/schema/schema-general.ts (source of truth).
- frontend/src/queries/schema.json, posthog/schema.py and services/mcp/src/api/generated.ts, all regenerated by `pnpm schema:build`. Do not hand-edit them.
- The runner WHERE in products/mcp_analytics/backend/hogql_queries/tool_tables.py.
- A per-runner case in `TestMCPToolDetailSharedFilters` in products/mcp_analytics/backend/tests/test_tool_tables.py. It runs unfiltered, then with a property filter, then with `filterTestAccounts` and `team.test_account_filters`.
services/mcp/src/tools/generated/mcp_analytics.ts is generated from products/mcp_analytics/mcp/tools.yaml. The PR left its regeneration to the CI bot, but the diff includes it.
applies: MCP analytics query kinds mapped in tools.yaml or sent by the frontend with shared filters.

Update the runner WHERE in products/mcp_analytics/backend/hogql_queries/tool_tables.py and add a per-runner case in posthog/mcp_analytics/backend/tests/test_tool_tables.py:TestMCPToolDetailSharedFilters covering unfiltered query, property filter, filterTestAccounts, and team.test_account_filters. The services/mcp/src/tools/generated/mcp_analytics.ts is generated from products/mcp_analytics/mcp/tools.yaml, and CI regenerates it, so the PR diff includes it.
